moments.title: Start with a known point
moments.text: Use $(2,2)$ on $y=f(x)$ to track what each transformation does to coordinates.

moments.title: Translations
moments.text: A translation shifts every point horizontally or vertically.

moments.title: Combine translations
moments.text: For $f(x+1)+4$, move the original point left $1$ and up $4$ to $(1,6)$.

moments.title: Vertical stretch
moments.text: For $3f(x)$, multiply every output by $3$; $(2,2)$ moves to $(2,6)$.

moments.title: Horizontal scale factor
moments.text: For $f(2x)$, halve each input coordinate; $(2,2)$ moves to $(1,2)$.

moments.title: Reflection in the horizontal axis
moments.text: For $-f(x)$, negate the output coordinate; $(2,2)$ moves to $(2,-2)$.

moments.title: Reflection in the vertical axis
moments.text: For $f(-x)$, negate the input coordinate; $(2,2)$ moves to $(-2,2)$.

moments.title: Review transformation cues
moments.text: The presenter summarises the inside/outside distinction, stretches and reflections.

notes.title: Horizontal scale is reciprocal
notes.text: To preserve the old input $u$ in $f(bx)$, solve $bx=u$. The new coordinate is $u/b$, so a factor of $2$ inside produces a horizontal scale factor of $1/2$.

notes.title: Follow a point for combinations
notes.text: For $y=a f(b(x-h))+k$, solve $b(x-h)=u$ for the new input and apply the output changes to $v$.

ican.text: I can describe horizontal and vertical translations, stretches and reflections.
I can map points through individual and combined transformations.
I can determine transformed domain, range and key features.
I can write an equation for a transformed graph and explain the effect of transformation order.

ku.text: For $y=f(x-h)+k$, each point $(u,v)$ maps to $(u+h,v+k)$: translate right $h$ and up $k$, using signed values.
For $y=af(x)$, each output is multiplied by $a$. If $a<0$, the graph is also reflected in the $x$-axis; distances from that axis scale by $|a|$.
For $y=f(bx)$ with $b\ne0$, each input coordinate is divided by $b$. The horizontal scale factor is $1/|b|$, with reflection in the $y$-axis if $b<0$.
For $y=af(b(x-h))+k$, an original point $(u,v)$ maps to $(h+u/b,av+k)$, provided $b\ne0$. This rule handles translation, scale and reflection together.
Transform endpoints and other key points to find a new domain and range. Reverse the order of inequality endpoints when multiplying by a negative number.
Order matters for transformations on the same axis. For example, $2(f(x)+3)=2f(x)+6$ is not generally the same as $2f(x)+3$.

misc.better: The same input to $f$ now occurs when the new input is $3$ larger, so the graph moves right $3$.
Each old input is produced by half as large a new input, so horizontal coordinates are halved.
It negates outputs and reflects in the $x$-axis. $f(-x)$ reflects in the $y$-axis.

misc.weak: Apply a vertical shift before scaling without checking the equation.
misc.better: For $af(x)+k$, scale outputs by $a$ first, then add $k$.

terms.text: A shift of every point through the same horizontal and vertical displacement.
A mirror transformation. Reflection in the $x$-axis negates outputs; reflection in the $y$-axis negates inputs.
A multiplier applied to distances from an axis. For $f(bx)$ the horizontal scale factor is $1/|b|$.

worked.prompt: A function $f$ has domain $[-2,4]$ and range $[1,5]$. The point $(2,3)$ lies on its graph. Define $g(x)=-2f(3(x-1))+4$.

parts.label: a
parts.q: Describe a sequence of transformations from $y=f(x)$ to $y=g(x)$.
parts.a: Horizontally compress by a factor of $\frac13$, then translate right $1$. Reflect in the $x$-axis and stretch vertically by a factor of $2$, then translate up $4$.

parts.label: b
parts.a: The point rule is $(u,v)\mapsto(1+u/3,-2v+4)$. Thus $(2,3)$ maps to $(\frac53,-2)$.

parts.label: c
parts.q: Find the domain and range of $g$.
parts.a: For the domain, $-2\leq3(x-1)\leq4$, giving $\frac13\leq x\leq\frac73$. For the range, $1\leq f\leq5$ maps under $-2f+4$ to $-6\leq g\leq2$. The endpoints reverse under multiplication by $-2$.

parts.label: d
parts.q: Explain why $-2(f(3(x-1))+4)$ gives a different vertical translation.
parts.a: Expanding gives $-2f(3(x-1))-8$. The $+4$ is inside the multiplication, so the final shift is down $8$, not up $4$.

kq.model: To produce the old input $u$, solve $2x=u$, giving the new input $u/2$. Every horizontal coordinate is halved.

kq.q: How can you check the direction of a horizontal shift?
kq.model: Choose an original input $u$ and solve the new inside expression for the input that gives $u$.

kq.q: Why can the order of transformations matter?
kq.model: Scaling also scales an earlier translation on the same axis. Follow points or expand the expression to check the order.
